Q0241

“All our dignity consists, then, in thought.” — Blaise Pascal (Pensées §347 (Brunschvicg))

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with Pensées §347 (Brunschvicg), within the Christian Existential Precursor tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of dignity, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Blaise Pascal's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
